body.p: At the end of the afternoon, the group returns to a familiar subject: nature, utility, and the problem of trust. A hand rests on a chair while someone reads aloud. Baruch Spinoza
The argument is not grand. It is built from ordinary words—bread, labor, memory, and observation—and that is enough for a clear summary. skepticism enters the room with calm precision. David Hume
Even a simple conclusion can open a larger view of the world. The day ends with quiet attention and the sound of closing pages. collective work lingers in the final line.
